chunks: I got married in Medina, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'How do you find her?' I said, 'Whatever good a man may find in a woman, I have found it in her — but she betrayed me.' So he said: 'And what is it?' I said, 'She gave birth to a girl.'
Verily, Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: 'your parents and your children — you know not which of them is nearer to you in benefit.'

key_terms.جارية: Girl, young female; also used for a female slave; here meaning a newborn daughter
key_terms.خانتني: She betrayed/failed me; the narrator's use of this word reveals his disappointment at having a daughter rather than a son
key_terms.عزَّ وجلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a common honorific for God (Allah 'azza wa jalla)
key_terms.نفعاً: Benefit, usefulness; the Quran emphasizes that we cannot know which of our relatives will benefit us most

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about having daughters in Islam?
ai.summary: A man complains to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that his wife 'betrayed' him by giving birth to a daughter, implying he had hoped for a son. The Imam gently corrects this attitude, quoting Quran 4:11 to remind him that God alone knows which child or parent will bring greater benefit — daughters should not be devalued. This hadith reflects the Imam's pedagogical approach of using Quranic verses to correct cultural biases against daughters inherited from pre-Islamic Arab custom.
